summary.headline: Prostarm H1 FY27 revenue rose 62.3% YoY to INR 196 crore, but Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 7.83% as costs and low-margin third-party sales weighed.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 82% YoY to INR 120 crore, but EBITDA fell 17% YoY to INR 9 crore with margin at 7.83%, and PAT fell about 27% to INR 6 crore (5.08% margin). Management attributed margin compression to low-margin third-party power and other product sales, higher freight (said to have almost doubled), forex impact on fixed-price contracts, higher employee and overhead costs, and start-up costs of the Bhachau and Bakrol plants. Order book stood at about INR 1,121 crore across 97 projects at 30 September 2026, with 78% government. Working capital cycle lengthened to 192 days from 185 days, mainly on receivables and inventory build, and operating cash flow remained negative.

financial_highlights.value: Net cash of about INR 97 crore cited versus about INR 105 crore borrowings-linked figure as stated; unclear on transcript

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: About INR 178 crore of the order book (about 16%); selective, high-value solar EPC work is being taken, with volumes elevated in FY27 but expected to moderate in FY28 unless high-value orders are won.

segments.name: Developer / BESS projects
segments.commentary: Developer projects of about INR 854 crore (government, 12-year annual rental of about INR 62 crore) and total VSS/EPC/developer book of about INR 999 crore (about 81%). Management is in talks to downsell two developer projects to a buyer.

segments.name: Manufactured power solutions (UPS)
segments.commentary: Order book about INR 26 crore; Bakrol UPS plant (about 3,000 pieces per day, 1 kVA to 600 kVA) can generate about INR 500-600 crore revenue per year at full utilisation.

segments.name: Third-party power and other products
segments.commentary: Low-margin third-party sales contributed to margin dilution in Q2 FY27; management said one third-party billing was executed in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 500 crore, based on about INR 266 crore order in hand plus about INR 20-25 crore of monthly billing additions.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided to remain above 11%, lower than the earlier 13-14% range; management described it as a moderation with FY27 revenue growth expected to be strong.

FY28 guidance: revenue growth of about 25% described as a minimum expectation; EBITDA margin expected to recover toward 12-13% and later about 18%; BESS-led margin of 8.5-9% described as achievable if BESS volumes come through.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by year-end FY27; management described this as a target rather than a commitment.

Bhachau BESS plant (1.2 GWh, single shift, scalable to 3 GWh on three shifts) expected to contribute from FY28; BESS capacity utilisation expected at 25-30% in FY28, with peak utilisation in about three years.
capex_capacity: Bhachau, Gujarat: 1.2 GWh BESS assembly plant, single shift, scalable to 3 GWh on three shifts; about INR 1,000 crore potential revenue per year at full utilisation.
Bakrol, Gujarat: UPS assembly facility with lithium integration, about 3,000 pieces per day; potential INR 500-600 crore per year.
Both facilities commenced operations on 25 September 2026; Bakrol expands UPS capacity across the 1 kVA to 600 kVA range.
Inventory rose to about INR 120 crore from about INR 77 crore to support new plant output and lead times (BESS lead time over three months).
Lithium cells will still be imported; BESS assembly is in-house but no backward integration yet.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR 1,121 crore across 97 ongoing projects at 30 September 2026; 78% government, 22% private.
Management cited India BESS market growth of more than 8x between FY25 and FY34 and data centre capacity rising from about 1,150 MW (December 2024) to about 3,200 MW by FY30.
Government VGS scheme (about INR 14,500 crore, 30 GWh) with about 40% local content requirement, and a PLI of 10 GWh, cited as support for domestic BESS manufacturing.
Management says pricing pressure is high from new entrants in BESS and UPS; it is shifting to selective tenders with high ticket size and private/channel business.
Average BESS order ticket about INR 40-50 lakh; utility-scale solar pricing pressure described as continuing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13-14% FY27 EBITDA margin still achievable, and what is the H2 margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margin would be above 11% and H2 would see moderation in costs; freight roughly doubled and forex hit fixed-price contracts. It has about INR 266 crore order in hand for FY27 revenue of about INR 500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin decline temporary or structural, and how will working capital and receivables evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it temporary, linked to low-margin third-party sales and start-up costs at new plants. Average receivable days were about 100 (about 178 excluding one large September billing of about INR 86-90 crore). Receivables fell from INR 257 crore at H1 to INR 201 crore in October 2026 after about INR 73-75 crore of collections.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking to downsell its developer projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in discussions with about six to seven industry players to sell down its two developer projects; no timing given beyond possibly this or next quarter. Equity IRR on these projects was said to be above 12% before margin erosion from lithium and dollar costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS capacity ramp and when will scale benefits show?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhachau plant (1.2 GWh single shift) is expected to contribute from FY28 with 25-30% utilisation next year; peak utilisation expected in about three years. Export samples of about 16 kWh units shipped to an overseas customer, with volume expected next financial year if approved.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company differentiate as BESS and solar become more commoditised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it focuses on local content, technical solutions, and OEM/technology partner positioning rather than a typical EPC; it is targeting selective tenders above INR 5 crore and private sector channel partners.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on FY28 BESS volume ramp and cost normalisation (freight, forex, lithium); management's margin guidance has been revised down from 13-14% to above 11% for FY27.
Working capital cycle at 192 days and negative operating cash flow (about INR -17 crore at September 2026 per management) remain key watch items.
Possible sale of two developer projects (INR 854 crore book) may create margin depletion and changes to the order book.
Competitive pricing pressure from new entrants and rising input costs in BESS and UPS.
Collection of about INR 201 crore receivables, including two large parties expected by December 2026.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand and order visibility but openly cautious on margins, acknowledging earlier margin guidance was too high and the current market requires taking lower-margin orders. Answers on working capital and cash flow were detailed but partly qualitative, and the company declined to give long-term margin targets or name export customers.
key_quotes: Our focus was on delivering numbers. Even if the margin is on the lower side, important for us to have the regular billing done on the books.
We would try to maintain Paras G, but still it should be above 11 percent.
So 25% is a minimum expectation that we are keeping an eye on a financial year.

adds.what: 1.2 GWh BESS assembly plant at Bhachau, Gujarat (single shift, scalable to 3 GWh on three shifts)
Bakrol UPS assembly facility with lithium integration, about 3,000 pieces per day (potential INR 500-600 crore/yr)

growth.why: FY27 revenue target of about INR 500 crore is backed by INR 266 crore order in hand plus INR 20-25 crore monthly billing (order book INR 1,121 crore), and FY28 revenue growth of about 25% is guided as a minimum, with Bhachau BESS (1.2 GWh) and Bakrol UPS plants started 25 Sep 2026 but BESS utilisation only 25-30% in FY28; FY27 EBITDA margin guide cut to above 11% from 13-14%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 7.83% and FY27 guide cut to above 11% from 13-14%; margin recovery to 12-13% in FY28 depends on BESS volumes, with BESS utilisation only 25-30% in FY28.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bhachau 1.2 GWh BESS plant and Bakrol UPS plant (about 3,000 pieces/day, potential INR 500-600 crore/yr) both commenced operations on 25 September 2026, with BESS contribution from FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue target of about INR 500 crore backed by INR 266 crore order in hand plus INR 20-25 crore monthly billing, and FY28 revenue growth of about 25% guided as a minimum from an order book of INR 1,121 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Both new plants only started on 25 Sep 2026 with BESS utilisation at 25-30% in FY28, so near-term new capex is not indicated; no new capex was announced or discussed beyond these.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was cut from 13-14% to above 11%, and management acknowledged earlier guidance was too high.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight nearly doubled, forex hit fixed-price contracts, and BESS utilisation guide was cut to 25-30%; working capital at 192 days and operating cash flow of about INR -17 crore add risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Export samples of about 16 kWh units shipped to an overseas customer, with volume expected next financial year if approved; no firm product launch date given.

rows.label: Working capital cycle at 192 days, receivables down to INR 201 crore
rows.why: Receivables fell from INR 257 crore at H1 to INR 201 crore in October after INR 73-75 crore collections, with two large parties expected to pay by December 2026, but cycle lengthened from 185 to 192 days and operating cash flow was about INR -17 crore.

rows.label: Sale of two developer projects (INR 854 crore developer book)
rows.why: Management is in talks with six to seven industry players to sell down the two developer projects, which could reduce the INR 999 crore VSS/EPC/developer book (about 81% of orders) and may deplete margin.

rows.label: BESS and UPS pricing pressure from new entrants
rows.why: Management says pricing pressure is high from new BESS and UPS entrants and utility solar pricing pressure continues, with the company shifting to selective tenders above INR 5 crore to protect margins.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, order visibility and the new plants, but cautious on margins, openly cutting FY27 EBITDA guidance to above 11% and calling the margin decline temporary; analysts pushed on margin trajectory, receivables, working capital and the developer project sell-down.
